construction_tiers.source: BFA24 Fig 33 (blended by prototype) and Fig 34 (by type: Type V $350, Type III $400, Type I $550 /gsf); code limits: WoodWorks Mid-Rise Design (2018 IBC Ch. 5), 2022-07-27

tiers.name: Type V (wood)
tiers.basis: BFA24 4-story prototype $350; Type VA limit 4 stories / 70 ft

tiers.name: Type V over Type I podium
tiers.basis: BFA24 6-story prototype (Type V over a Type I podium) $360

tiers.name: Type III over Type I podium
tiers.basis: BFA24 8-story prototype (Type III over Type I) $449; Type IIIA limit 85 ft, high-rise rules above 75 ft

construction_tiers.band_note: low = -10% (Part 2's hard-cost band); high = +18%, the low end of BFA24's 18-25% adder for Berkeley's labor standards (HARD HATS / Southside) on non-union projects
construction_tiers.cross_check: Part 2's cited series (Terner 2018 $332 x TBD index) is ~$509/gsf in 2025 for non-Type-I; times Part 2's fitted Berkeley factor (0.774) it is ~$394, inside BFA24's $360-449 mid-rise range

floor_to_floor_ft.source: labeled: 15 ft retail ground floor, 10 ft residential floors (8 stories = 85 ft, the Type IIIA limit, as in the 8-story staff reports: 2015 Blake 88.5 ft, 2435 Haste 90 ft)

retail_shell_cost_per_gsf_2024.source: BFA24 Fig 34: Retail - Type I $200/gsf; tenant improvements $100/nsf (not modeled: assumed paid by tenants)

berkeley_fees.source: City of Berkeley, Development Fees and Affordability Requirements, updated 2026-08-06 (Reso 72,418-N.S. adopted 2026-07-28); BFA24 Fig 37-38 for permit, plan check and other fees
berkeley_fees.legacy_ahmf_note: BMC 22.20.065 (AHMF, per unit) governs only projects vested on/before 2023-03-31; its current per-unit rate is NOT FOUND (2022: $46,185). The stalled projects approved before 2023 may fall under it.

bmr_rents_monthly.source: City of Berkeley BMR Program, Income and Rent Limits for 2025 (Exhibit A), Updated Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, effective 2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31: gross rents
bmr_rents_monthly.utility_allowance_note: BFA24 Figs 27-28 (2023): gross minus net = $100 (studio) to $235 (3BR); 1BR and 2BR interpolated (labeled)

construction_financing.source: rate: SOFR 30-day 3.89% (FRED, 2026-10-23) + bank construction spread 275-400 bp (CorAdvisors 2026-05; weak source); low = KMA Santa Cruz County 2026-05-21 6.2%; high = BFA24 8%. LTC 60% (KMA26), average outstanding 55% and 1 point (BFA24)
construction_financing.formula: interest = (hard + soft) x loan_to_cost x average_outstanding x rate x months / 12; + points x loan

legacy_ahmf_per_unit.source: City of Berkeley Council 2023-01-17 Item 21 (Rev2): 'the 2022 affordable housing mitigation fee ($46,185 per unit)'. Current rate NOT FOUND (City handout: 'contact HHCS'); 2022 rate used unescalated
legacy_ahmf_per_unit.formula: fee = A x FEE x (1 - (VLI + LI) / (0.20 x A)), floored at 0 (BMC 22.20.065; A = total units)

eli_rent_share_of_vli.source: ELI rent = 30% of 30% AMI / 12 vs VLI = 30% of 50% AMI / 12 -> 30/50 = 0.60 of the VLI gross rent (City Exhibit A income tiers)

height_search.source: labeled search range for the break-even height

efficiency.unit: net unit area / gross residential area

market_rent_multiplier.unit: multiplier on the Rent Board lease-up pool rents (record: JN-Feasibility Part 2a, 2022-24 lease-ups)
market_rent_multiplier.source: high: BFA24 Fig 26 6-story rents (CoStar + 10% new-construction premium) run 5-12% above the pool (studio $2,800 vs $2,495; 1BR $3,250 vs $3,056; 2BR $4,500 vs $4,295) -> +10%; low: -10% labeled (symmetric)

exit_cap_rate_today.source: base/high: CBRE Oakland multifamily infill Class A H1 2024 5.5-6.5% (Part 2's series, carried); low: BFA24 Fig 29 and Terner Making It Pencil 2023 (East Bay 2023), both 5.0%

yield_spread_over_exit_cap.unit: yield on cost needed above the exit cap rate
yield_spread_over_exit_cap.source: JN-Feasibility Part 1 Step 4b: the 100-150 bps rule of thumb

land_market_per_lot_sf.unit: $ per sqft of land, mid-rise development site
land_market_per_lot_sf.source: base/high: BFA24 Fig 34 land costs per sqft, 6-story $325 and 8-story $500 (prototypes sited in South & Southwest Berkeley); low: median of 30 corridor transfers 2021+ (record: data/derived/pencil_out/land_comps_corridor_2026-10-25.csv; quartiles $105/$149/$218)
land_market_per_lot_sf.caveat: the record comps are Prop 13 assessed values after a recorded document; a document that is not a reassessing sale makes the value stale (values under $50/sqft dropped as likely non-sales)

soft_costs_ex_fees_ex_financing.source: BFA24: soft costs 18% of hard (ex-fees) + developer contingency 5% + overhead 4% = 27%; low = 18% alone; high = Part 2's labeled 30%

operating_expenses_share_of_egi.source: low: BFA24 30% of gross scheduled income = 31.6% of effective income at 5% vacancy; base/high: Part 2's labeled 35% (40%). Base kept above BFA24 because it is unclear whether BFA24's 30% includes property tax on the new value (~1.2% of value)

iho_combination.source: City of Berkeley, Affordable Housing Requirements page (berkeleyca.gov, read 2026-10-28): projects may provide fewer than 20% of units as BMR (at least half VLI) and pay a prorated fee = $/sf RUFA x project RUFA x share of the requirement unmet by on-site BMR units; density-bonus projects pay on the base project's RUFA. Projects vested before 2023-04-01 follow the older requirements (legacy_ahmf_per_unit).
iho_combination.formula: fee = inclusionary_in_lieu_per_rufa_sf x net unit area x max(0, 1 - (ELI + VLI + LI) / (on_site_share x units))
iho_combination.applied_to: projects whose Planning application was filed on/after 2023-04-01 (filed date as the vesting proxy; an earlier SB 330 preliminary application could vest the older rules)
iho_combination.limitation: the base project's area is not in the record, so the full net area is used: overstates the fee for density-bonus projects

R-1.source: BMC 23.202.050 Table 23.202-2; Ord. 8007-N.S. s.1-2 (Middle Housing: multi-unit by ZC)
R-1.note: 22 ft within 15 ft of rear line; 60% lot coverage

R-2A.source: BMC 23.202.090 Table 23.202-9 per Ord. 8007-N.S. s.4; Middle Housing tabulation form 2025-10-27

R-1H.note: hillside: average 28 ft and 3 stories, maximum 35 ft

R-2H.note: hillside: average 28 ft and 3 stories, maximum 35 ft

ES-R.note: Environmental Safety-Residential (Panoramic Hill): single-family only, 25,000 sf new lots

R-3.note: OUTSIDE the Southside Plan. Inside: 45 ft, FAR 3.0, min 60 du/ac -- the layer has no Southside boundary, so every R-3 parcel gets the outside envelope (understates Southside R-3)

R-4.source: Corridors Existing Conditions Report (Raimi + Assoc., 2025-03-05) Table 5, via docs/audit/2026-08-12_czu_zoning_extract.md
R-4.note: 3 stories, no density or FAR cap per the 2025 report; 35 ft assumed from the 3-story limit; any use-permit height not known

R-5.note: average 40 ft and 4 stories; 65 ft and 6 stories with a Use Permit (not used). 40 ft fits 3 stories at 15/10 ft floor-to-floor

C-C.note: mixed use 40 ft and 3 stories; residential-only 35 ft and 3; FAR 3.0 read as the non-residential/mixed column

C-U.note: Avenue area (36 ft / 3 stories, FAR 2.2 north side). Node areas allow mixed use 48 ft / 4 stories, FAR 2.5-3.0; the layer has no node boundary, so every C-U parcel gets the Avenue envelope

C-E.note: RESIDENTIAL-ONLY envelope (35 ft, 3 stories, no FAR) -- more floor area than mixed use (28 ft, 2 stories, FAR 0.8 / 1.0 corner); residential-only lot coverage 40-50%

C-NS.note: RESIDENTIAL-ONLY envelope (28 ft, 2 stories, no FAR) -- more floor area than mixed use (35 ft, 3 stories, FAR 1.0)

C-SA.note: all parcels outside Subarea One; Subarea One allows 60 ft and 5 stories -- no boundary in the layer, so it is understated

C-SO.note: 28 ft and 2 stories for every use; FAR 2.0 mixed use, none residential-only

C-DMU Core.note: 75 ft with a Use Permit; up to five buildings 75-180 ft by Use Permit (Table 23.204-37); C-DMU FAR not checked

C-DMU Outer Core.note: maximum shares the Core row (60 ft; 75 ft with UP)

C-DMU Corridor.note: maximum shares the Core row (60 ft; 75 ft with UP)

C-AC.source: BMC 23.204.150 Table 23.204-44 (North and South Adeline, Tier 1)
C-AC.note: Tier 1 (<14% affordable). South Shattuck subarea Tier 1 is 45 ft / 4 stories, FAR 2.5, 120 du/ac -- no subarea boundary in the layer, so the Adeline envelope is used

MUR.note: residential or mixed use 35 ft / 3 stories; FAR 1.5 for buildings at least half residential; 1,250 sf of lot per unit = 34.8 du/ac

MRD.note: Manufacturing Research District: standards not read; treated as not residential

SP.note: Specific Plan area: standards set by the plan, not read

U.note: largely UC / state land outside City zoning

state_bonus.source: Cal. Gov. Code 65915(f)(2) (AB 2345, 2020): VLI 10% -> 32.5% density bonus
state_bonus.label: ASSUMPTION (waiver height = the bonus floor area stacked as stories)

sb79.source: ABAG, Senate Bill 79 (2025) Summary, last updated 2026-07-01, Table 1 (Gov. Code 65912.157); effective 2026-07-01
sb79.affordable: 11+ units: at least 7% ELI, 10% VLI or 13% LI on site; a higher local inclusionary requirement applies instead
sb79.density_bonus: SDBL applies on top, with SB 79 density as the base; no extra height beyond SB 79's (except 100% affordable)
sb79.labor: prevailing wage + skilled and trained workforce above 85 ft
sb79.exclusions: not on a site whose development demolishes rent-controlled housing occupied in the past 7 years (>2 units); cities may exclude very high fire zones and local historic sites until the 7th cycle

density_bonus.source: Gov. Code 65915(f)(2) as amended by AB 2345 (2020): 5% VLI -> 20%, +2.5 pts per 1% to 11% (35%), +3.75 pts per 1% to 15% (50%); the 2800 Telegraph plan set's table matches to 15%
density_bonus.ab1287_source: AB 1287 (eff. 2024-01-01), Gov. Code 65915(v): after the 50% bonus (15% VLI), additional VLI units earn an additional bonus; table per City of Los Angeles Planning, 2024-05-16 (data/assumptions/research/pencil_out_research_2026-10-25.yaml)

pipeline.story: Approved 2023-04-27 (ZAB) as 6 stories / 16 units under the State Density Bonus: 1 VLI unit bought a 27.5% bonus over a 12-unit base, plus waivers for height (70 ft vs 35 ft) and setbacks. Filed 2022-08-17 with an SB 330 preliminary application, so the pre-2023 affordable housing fee applies. The parcel sold in Dec 2025 (assessed $1.2M). Demolition permit B2026-00307 issued 2026-07-28; building permit application B2025-05618 is for 18 units, which is the plan set's own row for 2 VLI units / 15% / 50% bonus (12 x 1.5 = 18). v4 still shows 'entitled' (no building permit issued).
